To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have detected the first exoplanet orbiting a T Tauri star, that we have detected an exoplanet in the near-instrument, that we have found that the wavelength dependence of the RV amplitude can distinguish between spot-induced jitter and planet-induced RV signals, and that we have found three targets that show different periodicities at the two wavelengths.
we have developed a technique to search for young planets using RVs and that we have detected possible evidence for the presence of a giant planet around the young star GSC 06214.
we find evidence for different mechanisms causing the optical and K-band RV variations, and that we find evidence that the optical variations may be due to stellar spots.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a robust RV survey for the detection of giant planet companions to T Tauri and Herbig Ae stars.
identifying the most promising targets for future planet detection.
the detection of giant planet companions to young stars and the characterization of the RV jitter from young stars.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the RV jitter in the Taurus-AUR region is dominated by stellar spots and is not suitable for planet searches.
the majority of the Taurus T Tauri RV variability is not caused by planets.
the RV amplitudes of T Tauri star spots are significantly smaller in the near-intrared than at optical wavelengths.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are not detecting any giant planet hosts, but we are learning a great deal about the nature of T Tauri star spots.
the near-infrared is a promising avenue for the discovery of planets around T Tauri and Herbig Ae/Be stars.

, while the near-infrared RV method is a promising tool for detecting young exoplanets, the presence of strong stellar activity makes it difficult to distinguish between spot-induced RV modulation and the signal from a planet-multiple star systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
near-infrared RV surveys of young stars are possible and will be necessary to identify giant planet companions to T Tauri and Herbig stars.
the K-band can be an important tool in the RV search for giant planet companions to young stars.
the near-infrared offers a powerful tool for identifying and confirming young planet-mass companions.
